name: Proposal deck building
oneliner: The narrative and the artefact for presented pursuits, from executive summary to the version the committee reads without you in the room.
metaDescription: We build proposal decks for must-win pursuits: the storyline, the presented deck, the standalone reading version for evaluation committees, and the orals prep pack.

scenarios.title: Down to the final three
scenarios.text: You made the shortlist. The orals are in two weeks and the current deck is forty slides of product screenshots with no argument.

scenarios.title: The committee reads alone
scenarios.text: Half the evaluators never attend the presentation. They score the deck on their own screen, without your voiceover, and that score counts the same.

scenarios.title: Every deck starts from the last one
scenarios.text: The story is inherited from a different deal, patched by six people under deadline, and it reads exactly like that.

what: We build the deck for a presented pursuit, storyline first. That means the executive summary structure, the flow of the argument, the slide-by-slide build in your template, and a separate reading version designed to score well without a presenter, because evaluation committees score in private.
Your team presents it. We make sure what gets presented and what gets read both land.

deliverables.name: Storyline on a page
deliverables.desc: The argument of the deck, agreed and signed off before a single slide is built.

deliverables.name: Presented deck
deliverables.desc: The version your team performs in the room, built in your template and your voice.

deliverables.name: Reading version
deliverables.desc: The standalone version for evaluators who score alone, with the voiceover written in.

deliverables.name: Executive summary
deliverables.desc: The two pages a sponsor forwards upward when they want the deal approved.

deliverables.name: Orals prep pack
deliverables.desc: The questions this deck will provoke and who on your team answers each one.

steps.title: Bring the deal
steps.text: We read the response so far and the audience list, and tell you what the deck has to prove.
steps.need: The meeting invite and who scores

steps.title: Storyline
steps.text: The whole argument on one page, agreed before slides exist. Cheap to change here, expensive later.
steps.need: An hour with the deal owner

steps.title: Build
steps.text: We draft slide by slide in your template, with every claim traced to something true.

steps.title: Pressure test
steps.text: We tear it down the way a committee would, then rebuild the pages that failed.

steps.title: Hand over
steps.text: Presented version, reading version, executive summary, and the orals pack, delivered together.

excludes: We do not rebrand you. The deck lands in your template and visual identity.
We do not present to your buyer. The room is yours.
We do not invent claims or metrics to fill a slide. Thin proof gets a different argument, never a fabricated one.
We do not build the product demo. The deck frames it; your team drives it.

shape.v: One to three weeks, matched to the orals date
Retained, for teams with a steady shortlist rate

domains.name: B2B SaaS
domains.note: Product demos dominate SaaS orals. The deck's job is the argument a demo cannot make: risk, adoption, and the commercial logic.

domains.name: IT services
domains.note: Services deals are people deals. The deck has to make a team and a method feel as concrete as a product.

domains.name: BFSI
domains.note: Committees are larger and risk officers score too. The reading version and the risk pages carry extra weight.

domains.name: Healthcare
domains.note: Clinical and compliance stakeholders read differently. Jargon gets translated or it gets marked down.

related.desc: The written answer that earns the invitation to present.
related.boundary: The RFP is the written answer. The deck is the room performance. One narrative, two artefacts.

related.desc: The win themes the storyline is built on.

related.name: Startup pitch deck building
related.desc: The same craft aimed at investors instead of enterprise buyers.
related.boundary: Proposal decks win a buyer. Pitch decks win a round. Same discipline, different audience.
